ambiguities.source_text: MiniBytes want one output to be able to see, for each month:
ambiguities.intent: Report all 12 months January through December 2023 using each month's first day. Revenue uses the corrected sale month; all return metrics use the corrected return month. A month with no returns has missing Total Returns Value, Number of Returns and Avg Days to Return, not zeros. DD/MM/YYYY and equivalent ISO calendar dates are accepted; final row order is unrestricted.

ambiguities.source_text: Calculate the number of days between the Date Sold and Date Returned
ambiguities.ref: df["Days to Return"] = (df["Date Returned"] - df["Date Sold"]).dt.days
ambiguities.intent: After correcting reversed dates, subtract Date Sold from Date Returned to obtain an integer calendar-day count. Input dates are DD/MM/YYYY.
A missing return date means no return: days and refund are missing, and the row contributes only to sales revenue.
ambiguities.source_text: Calculate the number of days between the Date Sold and Date Returned
For returns within 60 days, customers get a full refund.
ambiguities.intent: Refund the full price for days <= 60, half the price for 61 through 100 inclusive, and zero for days > 100. A returned item with no refund still counts as a return.

ambiguities.source_text: customers will be refunded half (rounded to the nearest penny)
ambiguities.intent: Round each half-price refund to the nearest penny before monthly aggregation using ordinary half-up rounding. Exact halfway values round up: 1.985 becomes 1.99 and 1.995 becomes 2.00. Ties-to-even is not accepted. Use the same half-up rule for the final Revenue, Total Returns Value and Avg Days to Return at two decimals. Number of Returns is an integer count; numeric trailing zero padding is not required.
